chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — both from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara — who said:
When the water is more than a rawiya, nothing will render it impure — whether something has decomposed in it or not — except if a smell comes from it that overpowers the smell of the water.

key_terms.تَفَسَّخَ: tafassakh — decomposed, dissolved, or disintegrated (referring to a corpse or filth falling into and breaking apart in the water)
key_terms.رَاوِيَةٍ: rawiya — the water carried by a laden camel, used as a measure of volume in jurisprudence; classical jurists estimated it at approximately 384 litres
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: yunajjishu — to render something ritually impure (najis); the hukm of najasa has major consequences for ritual prayer and worship

ai.seo_question: How much water is needed to prevent ritual impurity in Islamic law according to the hadith of Zurara in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the fiqh ruling on large quantities of water and ritual impurity (najasa). The Imam (AS) states that water exceeding a 'rawiya' — approximately the volume carried by a laden camel, estimated by classical jurists at around 384 litres — cannot be made impure by the mere presence of filth, including decomposing matter. The sole exception is if the impurity so alters the water's smell that the smell of impurity dominates over the natural smell of the water. This ruling was of great practical importance in a desert context where water was a scarce resource, and it reflects the broader principle that large bodies of water are resistant to impurity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara,

‘Heasws said: ‘When the water was more than a Rawiya (a camel load of water), nothing would pollute it, whether something has fallen into it or not fallen into it, except if a smell comes from it, taking over the smell of the water’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “

If the quantity of water is more than a Rawiyah, then it does not become unclean because of things falling in it, regardless of whether they have disintegrated or not, unless the smell of such things overwhelms the smell of water.”
